segments.text: Page sixty-five reading. What kind of poems do you like to read? What are the names of the poets that you like? Khalil Gibran, poet, artists, and encourager. Khalil Gibran is one of the most famous poets in the world, second only to Shakespeare and Lao Tzu. He was born in Lebanon in eighteen eighty-three to a Catholic family, and he lived much of his later childhood and early adult life in the United States.
Surprisingly, Gibran had no formal schooling in Lebanon, but priests did visit his house to teach him religion and the Arabic and Syriac languages.
He later went to school and college in America. He was named College Poet at his university.

Gibran wrote both poetry and prose. He wrote first in Arabic and later began writing in English, quickly becoming popular internationally. His best-read book is The Prophet, which has been translated into forty languages and never gone out of print since its first printing in nineteen twenty-three. Gibran wrote about love, religion, and friendship, but he is best known for his skills and ability to encourage readers of many different backgrounds. Gibran had a caring heart for all people. He did a great deal to make his poetry meaningful and helpful to others. In one of his book, he says that half of what he said would probably not be remembered, but he wrote it all so that the readers can remember the other half. He was an artist of many types of visual art, poetry, prose, and philosophy during his life, but he is remembered the most for his famous books of poetry and prose.
